locations.quote: Motivation/Objective: **Since some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the efort required to maintain the servers and migrate the CI service from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service.**
Problem Statement: **The interactive learning platform Artemis currently only supports setups with an external CI server.   The CI server should be migrated to the VC server.      Furthermore, it**

Proposed Solution: **GitLab CI is the CI system provided by the GitLab VC server. This system supports the provision of the build plan via the Artemis API, which makes it possible to update the build plan retrospectively, as the build plan is fetched from the API on each run.**

(Expected) Results: **We expect to use the bridge pattern to dynamically bind Artemis to the concrete implementation with GitLab CI.      The reduction in server load will mean that more universities, especially smaller ones with less capacity, will choose Artemis.**

Artemis currently supports Bamboo      1 and Jenkins  2 as a CI server for executing the tests.   This leads to additional server overhead, since the CI and the Version Control (VC) are running on diferent servers.
Additionally, the base build plan is copied once after the student started the exercise [Krusche18].
the build plans must be updated manually in the CI Server.            Especially in large software engineering courses this is nearly impossible.

In exams, it would be useful to change the student build plans after the submission date to frstly hide the test cases during the exam and only compile the code and secondly use a debug compiler not failing due to a simple syntax error.

visible.title: Paragraph mixes unrelated ideas

locations.quote: According to Grady Booch’s book Object-oriented analysis and design with applications integration should generally take place regularly, to avoid problems later on [Booch95].       Martin Fowler explains in his post  Continuous    Integration,  Continuous   Integration  as  a practice,  in which   each integration,  which **should take place at least once per day per developer, is build and tested with predefned test cases**.   In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17].

locations.quote:
**1)  Name:      Exercise work fow**

**2)  Participating actors: Bob: Instructor, Mary: Student**

**3)  Flow of events:**
   1.  Bob prepares the exercise via the web interface of Artemis and pushes the exercise code template, the test cases as well as the sample solution to the VC server [Krusche18].

locations.quote: Supervisors should be able to provide their own scientific writing guidelines as well as conventions on the style of theses and proposals. Based on these guidelines, the LLM can provide formative feedback that is restricted to the aspects they cover. Since guidelines may not already be in a suitable format, the LLM may first need to preprocess them into a structured representation it can act on.

Ethically, it is difficult to let LLMs grade a final thesis, as this constitutes normative feedback and requires close scrutiny. Formative feedback, on the other hand, is less critical since it serves as input for students to improve their work.

If a regression occurs or an issue persists across iterations, the previous feedback was likely hard for the student to understand and act on. A regression means an aspect that was previously fine has worsened, while a persistent issue means earlier feedback flagged the same problem and the student has not yet resolved it.

In such cases, the feedback tool should adapt its style, for example by being more explanatory, more verbose, or providing concrete examples that illustrate the desired outcome. Where the feedback tool repeatedly fails to communicate an issue, it should defer the discussion to the supervisor.

locations.quote: Integrating large language models (LLMs) to assist supervisors with non-content-related feedback could improve the thesis writing process. As Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group’s writing guidelines and generating automatic formative feedback [NM06]. This Reviewer covers exactly the repetitive, non-content-related layer of feedback that currently drains supervisors, freeing them to focus on specific content and on discussions with their students, which is key in mentoring environments [BBE10, NM06]. The quality of feedback improves as supervisors have more time to engage deeply with the thesis, leading to better outcomes overall. Additionally, supervisors can provide feedback faster, making the process more scalable.

Supervisors should be able to provide their own scientific writing guidelines as well as conventions on the style of theses and proposals. Based on these guidelines, the LLM can provide formative feedback that is restricted to the aspects they cover. Since guidelines may not already be in a suitable format, the LLM may first need to preprocess them into a structured representation it can act on. **Ethically, it is difficult to let LLMs grade a final thesis, as this constitutes normative feedback and requires close scrutiny.** Formative feedback, on the other hand, is less critical since it serves as input for students to improve their work.

Ethically, it is difficult to let LLMs grade a final thesis, as this constitutes normative feedback and requires close scrutiny. Formative feedback, on the other hand, is less critical since it serves as input for students to improve their work. The idea is that students interpret the feedback themselves and discuss it, either independently or with their supervisor. Therefore, it is less important that every output of the LLM is perfectly correct.

This approach supports several modes of feedback generation. In one mode, no LLM-generated feedback is produced at all and all feedback comes from the supervisor. Alternatively, the student can obtain instant feedback on their proposal or thesis directly from the LLM, while keeping in mind that the supervisor has not reviewed this output. A third mode combines both sources, as illustrated in Figure 2. In this combined mode, multiple specialized agents analyze specific parts of the thesis in parallel. The supervisor then aggregates and reviews the resulting feedback and adds their own feedback. Finally, the supervisor merges both sets and publishes them to the student.

If a regression occurs or an issue persists across iterations, the previous feedback was likely hard for the student to understand and act on. A regression means an aspect that was previously fine has worsened, while a persistent issue means earlier feedback flagged the same problem and the student has not yet resolved it. In such cases, the feedback tool should adapt its style, for example by being more explanatory, more verbose, or providing concrete examples that illustrate
the desired outcome. Where the feedback tool repeatedly fails to communicate an issue, it should defer the discussion to the supervisor.

locations.quote: In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17]. They introduced an newly developed learning method which shortens the time between theory, which is usually taught in the non-interactive lecture, and practice, which typically follows about a week later, so that less knowledge is lost [Krusche17]. The concept, called Interactive learning, makes it possible for students to transfer the new acquired skills to real, application-based use cases still during lecture [Krusche17]. In order to implement this idea, the lecture is **split up**

**into multiple iterations, each consisting of different phases [Krusche17]. First there is a theory phase, before the instructor shows an example to the students. After that the students can try out the concept themselves, before they get a sample solution and instant, but still individual feedback generated by the CI server. Afterwards it is possible to reflect about the newly learned approach. With this fundamental idea, later the assessment management system Artemis was built [Krusche18].**

locations.quote: I will build a platform on which any member of the chair requests time-limited access to any resource, a maintainer decides, and the access ends on its own.

I follow the object-oriented software engineering method of Bruegge and Dutoit, and Figure 1 shows the actors and use cases of the platform as a use case diagram in the Unified Modeling Language. I pursue four objectives:
I will replace the flat list of hosts and channels with a resource tree whose inner nodes are folders and whose leaves each carry a binding to one target system.
I will store the tree with a transitive-closure table of ancestor–descendant pairs and cap the fan-out, so that an approval on the root never reaches the whole infrastructure by accident.

I will define one connector contract that validates a binding, grants and revokes access, and optionally lists the current members, and I will implement the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors on it.
I will build declarative request forms whose fields, visibility conditions, and rules turn answers into requests for a resource path, a level, and a duration.

I will therefore split the approval: in the review step, the resource owner records a decision without changing Keycloak, and in the grant step, the super admin sets membership and expiry atomically, in bulk for a vetted queue.
I will compare the manual administrative actions and the time to working access with the current process.
I will attach a recertification interval to each resource, which its descendants inherit, and open a campaign whenever the interval elapses.
The thesis runs from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, and I divide it into iterations of two to four weeks.
Outcome: the correctness scenarios pass, and I measure the effort.

**I model** the resources as a tree whose folders pass maintainership, audit policy, and grants down to leaves bound to target systems.
**I implement** the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors, whose credentials administrators configure at runtime.

**I reach** this objective when each access disappears after expiry and, in a second run with the workflow engine disabled on purpose, the drift check reports the remaining SSH membership.
Keycloak gates its workflow API on a realm-wide administrative role that maintainers must not hold, so **I split** each decision into a review step.
**I reach** this objective when administrators perform fewer manual actions and requesters wait less than in the current process.
**I reach** this objective when the platform answers, for any grant, who requested it and why, who reviewed and granted it, when it ended, and who confirmed it since.
**I divide** the work into six iterations of four weeks, each ending with a vertically integrated increment that a user can try in the web application.
**I reserve** the final two weeks, from 18 to 31 March 2027, as buffer for features that slip from earlier iterations.

locations.quote: In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17]. They introduced an newly developed learning method which shortens the time between theory, which is usually taught in the non-interactive lecture, and practice, which typically follows about a week later, so that less knowledge is lost [Krusche17]. The concept, called Interactive learning, makes it possible for students to transfer the new acquired skills to real, application-based use cases still during lecture [Krusche17]. In order to implement this idea, the lecture is split up into multiple iterations, each consisting of different phases [Krusche17]. First there is a theory phase, before the instructor shows an example to the students. After that the students can try out the concept themselves, before they get a sample solution and instant, but still individual feedback generated by the CI server. Afterwards it is possible to reflect about the newly learned approach. With this fundamental idea, later the assessment management system Artemis was built [Krusche18].

**I will** replace the fat list of hosts and channels with a resource tree whose inner nodes are folders and whose leaves each carry a binding to one target system.
I will store the tree with a transitive-closure table of ancestor–descendant pairs and cap the fan-out, so that an approval on the root never reaches the whole infrastructure by accident.

**I will** compare the manual administrative actions and the time to working access with the current process.
**I will** attach a recertifcation interval to each resource, which its descendants inherit, and open a campaign whenever the interval elapses.

locations.quote: **I will** build a platform on which any member of the chair requests time-limited access to any resource, a maintainer decides, and the access ends on its own. **I follow** the object-oriented software engineering method of Bruegge and Dutoit, and Figure 1 shows the actors and use cases of the platform as a use case diagram in the Unifed Modeling Language. **I pursue** four objectives:
**I will** replace the fat list of hosts and channels with a resource tree whose inner nodes are folders and whose leaves each carry a binding to one target system.
I will store the tree with a transitive-closure table of ancestor–descendant pairs and cap the fan-out, so that an approval on the root never reaches the whole infrastructure by accident.

**I will** defne one connector contract that validates a binding, grants and revokes access, and optionally lists the current members, and **I will** implement the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors on it.
**I will** build declarative request forms whose felds, visibility conditions, and rules turn answers into requests for a resource path, a level, and a duration.

**I will** therefore split the approval: in the review step, the resource owner records a decision without changing Keycloak, and in the grant step, the super admin sets membership and expiry atomically, in bulk for a vetted queue.
**I will** compare the manual administrative actions and the time to working access with the current process.
**I will** attach a recertifcation interval to each resource, which its descendants inherit, and open a campaign whenever the interval elapses.

visible.title: Excessive use of first-person singular "I" throughout the proposal
visible.description: The guideline states to avoid "I" and to use "we" sparingly, only for the thesis approach. The student uses "I" in 16 instances across Sections 4, 5, and the AI Transparency Statement. For the thesis-approach sections (Objectives, Schedule), the student should replace "I will…" with "we will…" (used sparingly) or restructure sentences to make the platform or a component the subject (e.g., "The platform replaces the flat list…"). In the AI Transparency Statement, a passive or third-person construction is preferred.

locations.quote: **I** will build a platform on which any member of the chair requests time-limited access to any resource, a maintainer decides, and the access ends on its own. **I** follow the object-oriented software engineering method of Bruegge and Dutoit, and Figure 1 shows the actors and use cases of the platform as a use case diagram in the Unified Modeling Language. **I** pursue four objectives:
**I** will replace the flat list of hosts and channels with a resource tree whose inner nodes are folders and whose leaves each carry a binding to one target system.
**I** will store the tree with a transitive-closure table of ancestor–descendant pairs and cap the fan-out, so that an approval on the root never reaches the whole infrastructure by accident.

**I** will defne one connector contract that validates a binding, grants and revokes access, and optionally lists the current members, and **I** will implement the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors on it.
**I** measure extensibility by the size of the change that the webhook connector needs after **I** freeze the framework.
**I** will build declarative request forms whose fields, visibility conditions, and rules turn answers into requests for a resource path, a level, and a duration.

**I** will therefore split the approval: in the review step, the resource owner records a decision without changing Keycloak, and in the grant step, the super admin sets membership and expiry atomically, in bulk for a vetted queue.
**I** will attach a recertifcation interval to each resource, which its descendants inherit, and open a campaign whenever the interval elapses.
The thesis runs from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, and **I** divide it into iterations of two to four weeks.
each item names the objective it serves and the outcome that **I** demonstrate.
**I** used the following generative artifcial intelligence (AI) tool while preparing this proposal.

visible.title: First-person "I" used pervasively against the group's style rule
visible.description: The group's writing-style rules say to avoid "one", "I", and "our" (use "we" sparingly, only for the thesis approach). This proposal writes the body text systematically in the first person singular: the abstract ("I develop", "I evaluate"), Section 4 ("I pursue four objectives", "I model", "I implement", "I freeze the framework", "I split each decision", "I reach this objective when…" three times), and the Schedule ("I divide the work", "I reserve", "I deliver" in every iteration). Rewrite the recurring occurrences: use "we" for the thesis approach itself or, better, third-person subjects such as "the platform" (which the text already uses heavily and fits the style). The AI Transparency Statement may legitimately stay in first person.

locations.quote: In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which every grant carries an expiry date from the moment somebody requests it.

visible.title: Scientific book cited only via a store-page URL footnote

A scientific book is an acceptable bibliography source, so give it a proper entry (authors, title, edition, publisher, year, ISBN/DOI) and keep only a URL if additionally desired.
